Hi Mateo,

Hope you're well. We're approaching the end of our current term (MSA + order form) and would like to scope a renewal that covers our next 24 months. Key asks from Clearwater: a 2.5x capacity uplift for inference units (mostly embeddings + chat), a shortened termination notice (45 days), and an SLA credit carve-out for regional outage windows.

Proposed commercial: 24-month term starting 2029-10-01, expansion to start 2029-12-01 with staged billing. We're open to a one-time implementation credit to offset migration work.

Thanks — happy to take a call first thing Thursday if that helps.

Best,

Subject: Re: Renewal proposal + capacity uplift (Q4 deploy) — MSA redline review

Thanks for the ping. I've gone through Clearwater's annotated MSA and attached our counter-redline (MSA_Redline_v3.pdf). High-level notes: 

- Indemnity: Clearwater requests a broader indirect damages carve-out and an indemnity cap tied to 24 months' fees. We propose a compromise: liability cap of the greater of $1M or six months of average historic fees, and mutual IP carve-out within that.

- Data retention: Clearwater asks for 30-day KV cache retention. Redwood standard is 7 days for ephemeral caches and 90 days for logs. We can accept a contractual commitment to delete KV cache on request with a maximum 30-day retention for cached inference contexts, subject to operational constraints (indexing/backfill windows). Need product confirmation.

- New surcharges / price changes: their 60-day limitation is reasonable; we need a mutual clause that permits cost passthrough for third-party infra changes with 90-day notice.

Outstanding asks for the business: 1) confirm whether staged billing (start charge at ramp vs. deploy) is acceptable, 2) whether we can offer a one-time implementation credit up to $40k without leader approval.

I've marked the redline with comments (see Attachment). Next step: product/ops confirm retention language and Marissa confirm credit authority and proration approach.

Karthik
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Commercials
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: MSA_Redline_v3.pdf (pdf)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Priya Anand <priya@clearwater.io>
Date: Wed, 24 Jul 2029 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal + capacity uplift (Q4 deploy) — billing / credit ops

Quick note on billing and credits:

- Proration: For staged expansion, we typically invoice based on effective consumption tiers monthly with retrospective true-up. For contract language let's commit to staged billing with monthly reconciliations.

- One-time implementation credit: finance can approve up to $25k from deal desk. Anything above $25k requires Director-level approval. If the commercial asks for $40k, we need an approval request with expected ROI delta (ARR uplift).

- Start date vs. charge start: we prefer charge to start on the date of activation (first production inference) rather than sign date — aligns with usage and avoids credits. We'll put that in the order form language.

Marissa Cole
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Renewal proposal + capacity uplift — clarifications on retention & credits

Thanks for the fast turnaround. A few clarifications from our side (answers inline):

- Data retention: We can accept a contractual delete-on-request but need guaranteed deletion timelines (clear milestones). Our target is 30 days maximum. OK to accept the delete-on-request exception as long as full delete happens within 30 days.

- Liability cap: We'll accept a numeric cap but would prefer it to be tied to annual fees (24 months' fees is our ask). If Redwood can move to a flat $1.5M cap we can accept that as compromise.

- Implementation credit: the $40k request is to offset our integration contractor costs (est. $38k). If Redwood can do $30k that's workable for us.

- Billing: activation-based charges are fine as long as we get an initial test window (two weeks) at no charge for smoke tests.

We can live with staged billing / monthly reconciliation. If legal provides redlines that reflect these items we can get procurement to sign quickly.

Best,
Marco Ruiz
Director, Platform Engineering
Clearwater Systems
